open-question.question: The new dispatched-agent invariant covers both dispatched agents: does it constrain only what a dispatch prompt carries (what the orchestrator holds and the agent cannot fetch), or also forbid a dispatched agent any whole read of a tool-owned document, and if the latter, how does it leave the complete-task agent's whole read of TASKS_TODO.md (a file no tool owns) untouched?
open-question.recommendation: The ban belongs next to the allowance it narrows, inside the invariant that already governs the question document, where its scope to that one document is fixed by where it sits, so the dispatched-agent invariant stays a prompt-content rule true of both agents without qualification and complete-task's whole read of TASKS_TODO.md is never in reach; a tool-owned clause is empty for complete-task today and must dodge the test fixtures, and the narrowest-slice rule shifts meaning whenever a tool gains a subcommand.
open-question.alternative: The dispatched-agent invariant covers only what a prompt carries. The reading rule instead goes into the sole-writer invariant, right beside the reworded whole-file allowance: inline runners may read the question document whole, and dispatched agents reach it only through the tool. That makes one boundary sentence scoped to the tool's own document, so it never reaches `TASKS_TODO.md`. The ban sits next to the allowance it narrows and inside the invariant that already governs `open_questions.xml`. Its scope to that one document is therefore clear from where it sits. The complete-task agent is never mentioned and cannot be caught by it, and the new dispatched-agent invariant stays true of both agents without qualification. The rules on what a dispatched agent receives and what it may read end up in two different invariants (three, counting the return contracts). An editor changing an agent has to find and reconcile all of them. How cleanly the ban fits depends on how the allowance itself is worded, which is decided separately.

The new invariant covers only what a dispatch prompt carries: the orchestrator passes what it already holds and the agent cannot fetch itself. It says nothing about what an agent reads. The alternatives agent's ban on reading `open_questions.xml` whole lives only in that agent's own file, and in CLAUDE.md it follows from the reworded whole-file allowance, which names only the inline runners and so leaves dispatched agents out. The rule holds for both dispatched agents as written, and nothing changes for complete-task. Its prompt already carries only the task's `##` heading, and its whole reads of `TASKS_TODO.md`, `requirements.md`, and the pointer are never touched. There is no carve-out to write, and the invariant matches the Goal's first sentence exactly. The reading half of the milestone has no stated reason anywhere. Dispatched agents are excluded only because the reworded allowance leaves them off its list, which an editor can easily miss. So a later edit can bring back the alternatives agent's whole read (or add a new agent that does one), and no invariant visibly forbids it.

The invariant has two clauses. One limits what a dispatch prompt carries. The other says a dispatched agent reaches a tool-owned document (the milestone's question document) only through the tool, never by reading it whole. The second clause is keyed on the document's owner, so files no tool writes, such as `TASKS_TODO.md`, `TASKS_DONE.md`, `requirements.md`, and `milestones/README.md`, are outside it by construction, with no named exception. Both halves of the milestone get their reason recorded in one agent-scoped place. The complete-task agent needs no carve-out: its `TASKS_TODO.md` read is outside the clause because no tool owns that file, and the clause would still apply if a tool later took ownership of some other file. For complete-task the reading clause is empty today, since the completion procedure never opens the question document. So the claim that the invariant covers both agents is partly nominal. The clause also has to name the milestone's question document, not the filename `open_questions.xml`. Otherwise a completion task in this repo that edits `tests/fixtures/*/open_questions.xml` would read as a violation.

The invariant covers the prompt and adds a general reading rule: a dispatched agent fetches the narrowest slice a tool offers and reads whole only what no tool can slice. `TASKS_TODO.md` and `requirements.md` are left alone because no tool slices them. The question document is covered because `locate` and the new list flag slice it. It states the reason behind the whole milestone, keeping the agent's context small, as one general rule. It also extends to future tools without an edit: if a task-list tool later offers a per-task slice, the complete-task agent comes under the rule automatically. What the rule allows changes silently whenever a tool gains or loses a subcommand. So it cannot be checked against the text alone, and a new tool feature could quietly make an existing whole read in complete-task or the completion procedure a violation. It also pushes a reader to ask whether `requirements.md` should be sliced too, which the Goal explicitly keeps as a whole read.
